sections.title: Front matter

summary.text: Title, authors and affiliations (Monash University, UNSW, CSIRO's Data61, ANU) of a paper introducing WireGen, which fine-tunes generative LLMs on thousands of UI examples so that a brief design-intent description yields mid-fidelity wireframes. The abstract reports 77.5% significantly better wireframes than two in-context learning baselines and a user study with 5 designers; CCS concepts and keywords follow.

sections.title: Introduction

summary.text: Argues that wireframing is a common way to express UI design intent, and that mid-fidelity wireframes add real content and semantic icons to low-fidelity sketches at a higher cost in time and effort, which no previous work has streamlined. Introduces WireGen, which fine-tunes LLMs on Rico UI screens and view hierarchies to generate mid-fidelity wireframes from design-intent descriptions, then post-processes them with semantic icons, text typography and UI guidelines. Reports 77.5% significantly better generations than two in-context learning baselines, 84.5% against three ablation models, and a user study with five professional designers.

summary.text: Despite its heading, this block continues the related-work discussion of UI wireframing: tools from SILK to Photoshop, Sketch and Figma support low- to mid-fidelity wireframes, and human-AI co-creation systems such as Swire help designers find inspiration or generate layouts. The authors note that these still require designers to sketch a low-fidelity wireframe and add content, whereas their work generates mid-fidelity wireframes directly from a design-intent description; the block ends by opening subsection 2.2 on bridging natural language and UI screens.

sections.title: Prepare Dataset of UI Wireframes and Descriptions

summary.text: Builds a training set by treating Rico's 66k Android UI screens (9.7k apps, 27 categories) as mid-fidelity wireframes and pairing them with Screen2Words descriptions written by 85 professional labelers. Screens are converted to HTML plus a style sheet by a depth-first traversal of the view hierarchy, mapping native classes to HTML tags (Table 1) from the resource_id, class, text, content_desc and bounds properties, with absolute positioning for layout.

sections.title: Fine-tune Large Language Models with Best Practice

summary.text: Fine-tunes with descriptions as input and HTML wireframes as output, and details three sensitive choices: 1,000 training samples selected by app (191 apps, 27 categories) to avoid leakage; the GPT model Turbo (gpt-3.5-turbo), chosen as the most advanced and strong at understanding code; and hyperparameters of learning rate 0.1, batch size 256, 4 epochs, temperature 0.65, a 4,096-token maximum length and </html> as the stop sequence.

sections.extract: Since the LLMs are not specifically designed to understand the UI design patterns, we fine-tune the LLMs with the natural language description as the input and the UI wireframe in HTML syntax as the output (the same learning objective as the pre-trained model). sections.title: Transform Raw Generation into Beautiful UI Wireframe

summary.text: Post-processes the raw HTML into usable wireframes in three ways: semantic icons, chosen by prompting the LLM against a top-10 icon-semantics category derived by open coding 4,000 Rico icons; text typography, framed as an optimisation over wrapping and font size that minimises wasted block space; and heuristics for three UI-guideline flaws found in 100 generations, namely occlusion, duplication and out-of-bound elements.

sections.extract: After fine-tuning process, we prompt the LLMs with a simple description of design intent to generate a HTML syntax of mid-fidelity wireframes. sections.title: RQ1: Performance of Fine-tuning

summary.text: Compares WireGen with zero-shot and few-shot prompting (K of 1 to 2 examples) under identical settings. WireGen's generations were rated significantly better 85.5% of the time on average, while zero-shot and few-shot received 51.5% and 44.5% significantly worse ratings, with a Cohen's kappa of 0.32; zero-shot produced relevant elements without regard to layout, and few-shot improved layouts but generalised poorly.

sections.title: Results

summary.text: Turbo was rated significantly better in 76.5% of cases, against 11.5%, 10.5% and 1.5% for Curie, Babbage and Ada; Curie and Babbage mostly produced average wireframes and 81.5% of Ada's were rated significantly worse, with a Cohen's kappa of 0.28. Examples show Turbo generating more detailed elements, such as subtitles under titles, which the authors attribute to it being the most powerful model.

sections.title: Procedure

summary.text: In one-hour Zoom sessions, participants generated a login-page wireframe by editing a given prompt, then used WireGen freely on their own scenarios alongside other tools, and rated it on a 5-point scale: effective for inspiration (4.4), relevant to the prompts (4.0) and diverse (3.6). All judged it better than wireframe-sharing, layout-generation and text-to-image tools, and they asked for integration with design software as a plugin and for representative images in place of alt-text.

sections.extract: The user studies were conducted online via the Zoom platform. Each participant took about one hour to complete. sections.title: Discussion

summary.text: Names limitations and future work: training on only 1,000 samples for budget reasons, post-processing based on a small-scale study of design flaws, and prompts built only from screens and view hierarchies. Proposes multimodal prompts, iterative design through chat, and retrieving similar existing UI designs by encoding generated wireframes with Screen2Vec.

sections.title: Conclusion

summary.text: Restates that WireGen fine-tunes LLMs on thousands of UI screens and view hierarchies, generates raw wireframes from design-intent descriptions and post-processes them, and that experiments and a user study show it outperforms baselines and ablated models and is useful in practice.

sections.extract: This paper introduces WireGen, a new method for exploring human-AI collaboration in mid-fidelity UI wireframe creation. Inspired by the success of generative Large Language Models in creating innovative ideas, we purpose to inherit LLMs’ in-context ability from billions of web resources to create mid-fidelity UI wireframes.
